cases.architecture: Qwik City 1.12 storefront rendered by Vite SSR on the Node adapter, with a Postgres data layer reached through the pooled pg client in src/lib/db.ts and the customer session read from the signed vs_session cookie by src/lib/session.ts.
cases.why: The route loader returns result.rows from a `select m.*` join that carries gateway_payment_token, gateway_customer_ref, fingerprint, the billing address and the fraud team's analyst_note. Qwik serialises every loader result into the SSR payload, so all of those fields are shipped to the browser and sit in the page HTML even though the component paints only the brand and the last four digits.

cases.architecture: Qwik City 1.12 storefront rendered by Vite SSR on the Node adapter, with a Postgres data layer reached through the pooled pg client in src/lib/db.ts and the customer session read from the signed vs_session cookie by src/lib/session.ts.
cases.why: useStartActingAs is a routeAction$, which Qwik City exposes as a POST endpoint on /support/impersonate that any client knowing the URL can call directly. The body only checks that some session cookie exists and never consults isSupportAgent, so an ordinary signed-in shopper can post any customer email and have writeSession mint a session cookie for that account. The staff SSO proxy in front of the console is not in the request path for a direct POST.

cases.why: The same session-swapping route action, but authority is re-derived inside the action body: isSupportAgent(session) fails the request with 403 for anyone who is not an agent, and the ticket lookup additionally requires assigned_agent_id = session.customerId, so a direct POST from a shopper can never reach writeSession.

cases.why: event.params.invoiceNumber is joined straight into join(ARCHIVE_ROOT, 'invoices', session.customerId, `${invoiceNumber}.pdf`) with no shape check, and readFile then returns whatever that resolves to. Encoded `..` segments walk out of the per-customer folder, which is the only access control on this endpoint, so any PDF on the archive share -- including other customers' invoices -- is downloadable.

cases.architecture: Qwik City 1.12 storefront rendered by Vite SSR on the Node adapter, with a Postgres data layer reached through the pooled pg client in src/lib/db.ts and the customer session read from the signed vs_session cookie by src/lib/session.ts.
cases.why: event.params.reference and the sort, dir and limit query values are concatenated into the statement template that is handed to pool.query as a single string with no values array, so Postgres parses them as SQL. A reference containing a quote closes the string literal and lets the caller drop the customer_id predicate or union in other tables, which also defeats the per-customer scoping the comment claims.

cases.architecture: Qwik City 1.12 storefront rendered by Vite SSR on the Node adapter, with a Postgres data layer reached through the pooled pg client in src/lib/db.ts and the customer session read from the signed vs_session cookie by src/lib/session.ts.
cases.why: The same listing built the same way, but the reference, the session's customer id and the clamped limit are passed to pool.query as $1/$2/$3 bind parameters. The only interpolated fragments are a sort key resolved through the SORTABLE_COLUMNS allowlist and a direction narrowed to the literals asc or desc, so no caller-controlled text reaches the parser.

cases.why: delivery_notes.body_html is authored by whoever paid for the box, which for a gifted subscription is a different person from the recipient reading this page. The loader passes the column through unchanged and the component$ hands it to dangerouslySetInnerHTML, so third-party markup and its event handlers execute inside the recipient's authenticated account page.

cases.why: The same sender-authored HTML rendered through the same dangerouslySetInnerHTML sink, but every body passes through sanitize-html with the GIFT_MESSAGE_HTML options first: six inline tags allowed, an empty allowedAttributes map and no allowed URL schemes, so no event-handler attribute, javascript: URL or script element survives the loader.

cases.architecture: Qwik City 1.12 storefront rendered by Vite SSR on the Node adapter, with a Postgres data layer reached through the pooled pg client in src/lib/db.ts and the customer session read from the signed vs_session cookie by src/lib/session.ts.
cases.why: loadEarlierTicketMessages is a server$ function, so Qwik compiles it into a POST endpoint that any signed-in browser can call with arbitrary arguments. It authenticates the caller but then filters only on the client-supplied ticketId, with no predicate tying the ticket to session.customerId, so the support thread of any customer -- addresses, refund reasons, partial card data -- is readable by walking ticket ids. The neighbouring countOpenTickets shows the scoping the author omitted here.
